View tiers for every noun — and the seam that must fail closed

content.value: The presentation half of the context-compression program: one tier grammar for the whole content model, built as a projection of the

envelope — never the other way around. This paper ratifies a three-layer grammar with a sharp fieldful-vs-blobful boundary, delivers the security review of every new read path (emitter census, nil-polarity verdict, handle-resolution laws), and freezes the fail-closed proof obligation every epic slice must carry. Nothing was built this run — this is the plan a wave starts from instead of zero.

blocks.text: Where the evidence pushes back

content.value: The strongest argument against a

brief mechanism: brief card v2’s diet came from nine cuts a schema block cannot express (grapheme caps 96/160, claim signal-gating, omit-when-steady-state, seconds-precision timestamps). A declared field list will produce

blocks.text: Rev on the card — converging with the handle and flagship lanes

content.value: The one cross-lane contradiction this paper must help settle: brief card v2 was frozen

(charter D3; live-confirmed — today’s ready card is exactly 9 keys, none of them rev). The handle doctrine needs rev as the handle anchor on exactly that card; the flagship board wants rev on every card (~+9% bytes measured); and the rev-carriage census shows every brief surface drops it — task brief, search brief (hit_envelope.ex:106-131 drops a rev it already computed), MCP task_ready/task_prime — while the one full-view surface the TUI consumes sends rev that the Go client never decodes (fetch.go:194-219 has no Rev field). Three rival resolutions:

one card everywhere; the handle anchor rides every surface; +9% measured; no manifest change
reopens the frozen contract — @brief_keys exact-set test + both byte tripwires must be rewritten in the SAME PR
brief untouched; board tuning can undo the cuts that starve merges
unfreezes the 3-key manifest shape — charter law 7 demands a fresh opt-in dance; a third serializer to maintain

content.value: Add rev as an

(opaque 32-hex Document CAS — never ordered, never parsed), which also honestly fixes the flagship’s merge-starvation finding: staleness detection moves off the seconds-truncated (UpdatedAt, epoch) pair onto rev equality. And one grammar law lands with it, from the dual-rev census: unqualified
rev
always means Document CAS (32-hex); Papers’ monotonic content int is ALWAYS spelled
paper_rev / content.rev / --if-rev
and never abbreviated to bare rev in any new API surface — today no acceptor mixes them, but nothing legislates it. Final ratification of brief-v3-vs-board-profile belongs to the capstone/user.

blocks.text: Handle-resolution laws this lane binds (inherited by the handle-doctrine lane)

content.value: No (doc_id, rev) route exists on main — doc show needs dataset+type and serves only the current doc; revision show takes the revision ROW UUID (router.ex:2231, :2267). Whatever endpoint the handle lane designs inherits three laws from this seam:

children.value: Visibility at READ time, under the CURRENT schema.

items.value: The WS-B revision precedent (history_controller.ex:19-38): old snapshots hold plaintext of now-private fields; redaction is evaluated when read, never trusted from snapshot time.

children.value: The route lives INSIDE the scoped pipelines.

items.value: Fail-closure of scope_to_workspace_or_global depends on the workspace assign being present (scope_helpers.ex); a handle endpoint mounted outside ResolveWorkspace/AssignDefaultScope silently goes global. The epic pins the pipeline, not just the query — proven by a cross-workspace handle → 404 test.

Confirmed clean today: perspective (draft/published) is resolved once from AnonPerspective/CallerContext before retrieval; ?view= and ?fields= touch only post-retrieval shaping (query_controller.ex:19-99, search_controller.ex). Every new tier keeps this orthogonality, tested.

content.value: The undeclared-field-is-public legacy rule interacts badly with old revisions: a field deleted from the schema would UN-redact on a rev-pinned read (undeclared ⇒ public), while a field public at snapshot time but private now is correctly re-hidden — asymmetric. Candidate rule: on revision/handle reads, undeclared fields fail CLOSED (dropped), inverting legacy parity for historical snapshots only. Left explicitly to the user — it trades back-compat for safety on a surface with few consumers today.

blocks.text: Risks, unknowns, and the calls left to the user

content.value: (1) Declared briefs may be mediocre without per-noun tuning — mitigated by caps-in-declaration + mandatory tripwires + hand-tuned serializers staying legal, but the risk is real: the 20–80× wins were hand-measured. (2) Reopening the frozen brief card (rev add) touches a contract two shipped waves deliberately froze — the amendment discipline exists, but drift risk is nonzero. (3) The unsealed embed chain is latent only until someone marks a task field private — sequencing matters: seal before tiers. (4) This checkout carries uncommitted local modifications on exactly the files this lane names (board_live.ex, tasks/schema.ex, internal/taskboard/*) — the wave MUST re-survey main at build time; every anchor here is origin/main as of 2026-07-23. (5) All byte figures are 2026-07-18/23 snapshots — re-run the wc -c probes for fresh baselines rather than trusting them.

Judgment calls explicitly left open (the capstone/user ratifies): brief v3 rev-add vs a board profile (this paper recommends v3); flip-vs-fence on the nil clause (recommends both); seal query.ex now vs on-first-private-field (recommends now); the axi-b7 write-echo ruling (recommends ?view=brief opt-in); ?views=1 graduation (recommends staying opt-in); the schema-evolution rule for rev-pinned reads (no recommendation — a genuine trade); whether the views descriptor grows a machine-checkable full_via escape-hatch field (costs the frozen 3-key shape; recommends deferring).

No (doc_id, rev) route exists on main — doc show needs dataset+type and serves only the current doc; revision show takes the revision ROW UUID (router.ex:2231, :2267). Whatever endpoint the handle lane designs inherits three laws from this seam:

The undeclared-field-is-public legacy rule interacts badly with old revisions: a field deleted from the schema would UN-redact on a rev-pinned read (undeclared ⇒ public), while a field public at snapshot time but private now is correctly re-hidden — asymmetric. Candidate rule: on revision/handle reads, undeclared fields fail CLOSED (dropped), inverting legacy parity for historical snapshots only. Nothing was built this run — this is the plan a wave starts from instead of zero.

The capstone (/papers/ctx-compression-capstone) links all five lanes and files the considering-state epic candidate.

What we will create — a three-layer tier grammar, not a merge

Three tier mechanisms already coexist on main and do different jobs — transport contract, caller projection, UI card composition. The naive move (merge them into one) is refuted by the evidence: the task brief card’s 20–80× wins came from nine hand-measured cuts, not a field list, and list_preview (tasks/schema.ex:59) is a 2-slot badge+meta UI spec far too thin to be a brief composition. So the proposal is three layers plus one binding law, and a two-regime boundary shared word-for-word with the handle-doctrine lane.

Layer 3 is the only net-new mechanism. Because every fieldful noun (documents, media docs, sheets, tickets, tags) flows through QueryController, one implementation covers them all — while jargon-heavy nouns with bespoke controllers (task, search) keep their hand-tuned serializers exactly as shipped. Extension cost per noun is a manifest declaration plus server-side ?view= support: internal/cli/run.go resolveView (:250-275) is fully manifest-generic, so bp and the MCP bridge light up with zero Go changes.

The two-regime boundary (convergence sentence — the handle-doctrine paper states this in the same words) Fieldful nouns get views; blobful nouns get handles. A noun whose weight is spread across many fields earns a declared brief view. A noun whose weight is one body blob (paper, sheet) earns windowing and retrieval handles instead — field-dropping cannot compress a blob. The live census draws the line sharply: paper query is 153 KB/doc full and 346 B/doc at fields=title (the whole weight is .blocks); task is 5.7 KB/doc full → 335 B projected. Papers need block-level windowing and (doc_id, rev) handles — the handle lane’s territory — not a 13-field card.

Where the evidence pushes back

The strongest argument against a declared brief mechanism: brief card v2’s diet came from nine cuts a schema block cannot express (grapheme caps 96/160, claim signal-gating, omit-when-steady-state, seconds-precision timestamps). A declared field list will produce mediocre diets without per-noun tuning. The design answers this three ways: Layer 3 declarations carry caps, not just field names; every new noun’s brief ships behind the AXI byte-tripwire pattern (realistic + hostile ceilings, frozen in CI); and hand-tuned serializers remain legal — Layer 3 is the default, never a straitjacket. Live proof the ceiling is real: hand-tuned task.ready brief is 271 B/card vs 335 B/doc for generic fields=title — a further ~20% that only tuning buys.

SEAL → EXPAND → PROJECT is already shipped law on both existing paths: the doc path (query_controller.ex:348-358 — Envelope.render → Expand → project_fields) and the tasks path (Params.seal → Envelope.redact before render at every emission point in tasks_controller.ex — :97, :144-153, :368-373, all six mutation echoes, :817-818). The security review — what the seam census found

The storm ran a full emitter census over api/lib (78 controllers + plugin web modules + the task-embed chain) and a complete call-site classification of Envelope.render/redact/field_readable?. Headline: the seam is in far better shape than the 14-day-old memory suggested — the WS-B bypass vein is sealed and independently re-verified — but the census surfaced one genuinely unsealed chain, one live footgun, and one unlegislated class.

Finding 1 · The nil-polarity inversion is real — and dead

Envelope.field_readable?(_schema, _field, nil) ⇒ true (envelope.ex:222 — nil means UNRESTRICTED) while Envelope.render/3 treats nil as the anonymous, MOST-restrictive principal. Opposite polarities on sibling functions of the same module. The blast-radius census classified every caller: zero HTTP/WS-reachable call sites pass nil — every one passes from_conn, an explicit anonymous(), or the off-request :internal sentinel, and several (highlighter.ex:218, hit_envelope.ex:108) already distrust the default and guard caller_context || anonymous() locally. This is the fossil of the completed WS-B audit, not a live hole. But nothing structurally prevents the NEXT hand-rolled emitter — park receipts, a board serializer, a handle endpoint, all proposed by sibling lanes — from passing nil believing it fails closed.

OptionForAgainst

Severity today: latent — the task schema (schema.ex:51) is visibility:“public” with no private fields yet. But the epic builds its flagship (two-level task board) and new tiers directly on this mechanism, and prior art (ag-backlinks-grant-leak) shows the “one consumer sealed, sibling not” class recurs. Recommendation: seal query.ex NOW (defense-in-depth, copying board.ex’s gate verbatim), before any tier work stacks on it — with the redact-then-assert-omitted proof attached. The alternative (defer until a field goes private) is left as an explicit user call.

CycleFleetController.release_paper_source/render (cycle_fleet_controller.ex:112-185) emits raw content["blocks"] with zero Envelope references — tenancy/auth-gated only. Same shape as the onixedit/sheets export controllers, bulldocs_form (:114), media_processing (:43) and scoped_paper (:44). These read as intentional (export = “give me everything”), but none would inherit a future per-field privacy rule. The epic should not silently bless them: one slice writes the export-class law — every full-content emitter either routes through Envelope or carries a recorded, tested exemption. No third state.

Add rev as an equality-only change token (opaque 32-hex Document CAS — never ordered, never parsed), which also honestly fixes the flagship’s merge-starvation finding: staleness detection moves off the seconds-truncated (UpdatedAt, epoch) pair onto rev equality. Pulse-churn (rev bumps on every lease renewal) is handled by event-KIND-classed invalidation — a shared ruling with the handle and flagship lanes. And one grammar law lands with it, from the dual-rev census: unqualified rev always means Document CAS (32-hex); Papers’ monotonic content int is ALWAYS spelled paper_rev / content.rev / --if-rev and never abbreviated to bare rev in any new API surface — today no acceptor mixes them, but nothing legislates it. Final ratification of brief-v3-vs-board-profile belongs to the capstone/user.

Two rulings this lane owes the backlog

  • axi-b7 (write-endpoint views, open): claim/close echoes are full renders with a 510 B content.brief echo (22% of the payload). Position: Layer-1 views declarations extend to write commands — ?view=brief opt-in on mutation echoes, absorbing axi-b7’s option (a). The escape hatch stays: task.get never declares views.
  • ?views=1 graduation: left OPEN. Default emission would brick stale strict-decode binaries; graduating needs a manifest_version discipline that does not exist today. The opt-in stays; every new noun’s declaration hides behind it, by design.

Handle-resolution laws this lane binds (inherited by the handle-doctrine lane)

No (doc_id, rev) route exists on main — doc show needs dataset+type and serves only the current doc; revision show takes the revision ROW UUID (router.ex:2231, :2267). Whatever endpoint the handle lane designs inherits three laws from this seam:

  • Visibility at READ time, under the CURRENT schema. The WS-B revision precedent (history_controller.ex:19-38): old snapshots hold plaintext of now-private fields; redaction is evaluated when read, never trusted from snapshot time.
  • The route lives INSIDE the scoped pipelines. Fail-closure of scope_to_workspace_or_global depends on the workspace assign being present (scope_helpers.ex); a handle endpoint mounted outside ResolveWorkspace/AssignDefaultScope silently goes global. The epic pins the pipeline, not just the query — proven by a cross-workspace handle → 404 test.
  • Projection never widens rows. Confirmed clean today: perspective (draft/published) is resolved once from AnonPerspective/CallerContext before retrieval; ?view= and ?fields= touch only post-retrieval shaping (query_controller.ex:19-99, search_controller.ex). Every new tier keeps this orthogonality, tested.
Open judgment — schema evolution on rev-pinned reads The undeclared-field-is-public legacy rule interacts badly with old revisions: a field deleted from the schema would UN-redact on a rev-pinned read (undeclared ⇒ public), while a field public at snapshot time but private now is correctly re-hidden — asymmetric. Candidate rule: on revision/handle reads, undeclared fields fail CLOSED (dropped), inverting legacy parity for historical snapshots only. Left explicitly to the user — it trades back-compat for safety on a surface with few consumers today.

What we learned — evidence and surprises

  • The wish is a second wave, not a greenfield. Brief/tabular agent views across CLI+MCP+API already shipped (AXI epic, merged 2026-07-18/19, graded A-): manifest views contract, brief cards on three commands, 48 KB rune-safe MCP clamp, measured 12–92× wins. This epic extends a proven pattern by frequency×size ranking — it must not re-invent the mechanism.
  • Hand-tuning beats generic projection by ~20%. 271 B/card (task.ready brief) vs 335 B/doc (fields=title) — direct evidence for the interview’s bet that a deterministic render profile can beat a SmartCrusher port on our own data (caveat: different types — suggestive, not a controlled A/B).
  • The regime boundary is sharp. 442× on papers via fields=title vs 17× on tasks: blob nouns don’t want a card, they want windowing + handles.
  • The seam aged well. The field-visibility vein’s “mined out” memory claim is DEMOTED-NO-RERUN (belief-level), but the storm’s emitter census independently re-verified every named WS-B surface sealed — the belief is now grounded by fresh evidence, and the epic’s seam work is about NEW projections only.
  • The cheapest win in the whole program is an alias. Agents typed the nonexistent bp task show 2,428 times and bp task list 329 times in one project corpus — over 1.1 MB of pure error-response waste. A ‘did you mean task get’ hint or alias is a one-slice fix with measured payback.
  • criteria_met/criteria_total near-zero usage is NEWNESS, not deadness. They shipped 5 days before the census; do not cut them on this evidence — re-census in weeks.
  • 404-on-empty is a real gotcha. doc.query on a valid type with zero docs returns a 404 error body, not [] — any tier/park/board client assuming list-shape will mis-handle it. The epic should fix or at least document this at the contract level.
  • The two-level board already exists in Studio. board_live.ex is compact server-projected cards + a fresh per-doc peek read — the flagship formalizes a live precedent; the TUI (full corpus, no view param, 32 MiB ceiling) and mobile (greenfield, zero fetch code yet) are the adopters.

Risks, unknowns, and the calls left to the user

Risks the wave inherits (1) Declared briefs may be mediocre without per-noun tuning — mitigated by caps-in-declaration + mandatory tripwires + hand-tuned serializers staying legal, but the risk is real: the 20–80× wins were hand-measured. (2) Reopening the frozen brief card (rev add) touches a contract two shipped waves deliberately froze — the amendment discipline exists, but drift risk is nonzero. (3) The unsealed embed chain is latent only until someone marks a task field private — sequencing matters: seal before tiers. (4) This checkout carries uncommitted local modifications on exactly the files this lane names (board_live.ex, tasks/schema.ex, internal/taskboard/*) — the wave MUST re-survey main at build time; every anchor here is origin/main as of 2026-07-23. (5) All byte figures are 2026-07-18/23 snapshots — re-run the wc -c probes for fresh baselines rather than trusting them.

Judgment calls explicitly left open (the capstone/user ratifies): brief v3 rev-add vs a board profile (this paper recommends v3); flip-vs-fence on the nil clause (recommends both); seal query.ex now vs on-first-private-field (recommends now); the axi-b7 write-echo ruling (recommends ?view=brief opt-in); ?views=1 graduation (recommends staying opt-in); the schema-evolution rule for rev-pinned reads (no recommendation — a genuine trade); whether the views descriptor grows a machine-checkable full_via escape-hatch field (costs the frozen 3-key shape; recommends deferring).

Coverage appendix — checked and found, checked and NOT found

Found (grounded, with rerun paths)

  • AXI ground truth read in full: charter + both wave papers + ergonomics review — rulings, byte tables, tripwires, backlog states verbatim; axi-b6 + the batch If-Match hole are FIXED on main (both halves of the rev-fencing seam closed); axi-b4/b7 open + unclaimed; R6/R8/R9/R10 charter-text only, never filed as tasks
  • Envelope/CallerContext/scope_helpers/tenancy contract, seal ordering on both paths, HitEnvelope, revision redaction — all at file:line on origin/main
  • Full emitter census (78 controllers + plugin web modules + the embed chain) with seal verdicts; full nil blast-radius classification (0 HTTP-reachable nil callers)
  • Live byte census on guerrilla (admin tier, production dataset): 7 nouns + the live brief-card key list (9 keys, no rev)
  • Protective-test inventory: 40+ tests catalogued into the 6-pattern proof template; transcript census 15,829 files / 1.35 M lines, 0 parse errors
  • Surface parity: JS SDK fields=/expand= plumbing exists (doc.ts, filter-builder.ts); Studio board two-level split already live; TUI + mobile adoption states pinned

NOT found — absences are decisions-in-waiting

  • No (doc_id, rev) resolution route exists on main — the handle endpoint is genuinely greenfield (router.ex:2231, :2267)
  • No rev key on ANY brief surface (live-confirmed) — the handle anchor does not exist yet
  • No ruling anywhere on whether views.supported may grow beyond [brief,full] — open by silence, not settled
  • No dedicated hit_envelope_test.exs — indirect coverage only; flagged as a gap the epic closes
  • No /admin/projects LiveView route found despite the memory note saying W1-W5 merged — unresolved discrepancy; re-grep before the flagship builds
  • No private task field exists today (schema.ex:51 public) — the unsealed chain is latent, which is exactly why it is cheap to seal NOW
  • No fields=/projection census on media.ls, tag.browse, ticket.inbox; no bp park prior art anywhere (closest: workspace-bundle export/import)
  • ~24 controllers with zero content-grep hits were NOT individually opened (delegated serializers would evade the grep); sibling_controller_leak_test.exs + studio_scope_p0_test.exs not opened; ~82 non-barkpark transcript dirs not censused
  • TaskResolver fetch-fn wirings traced for the two live consumers only; the DEMOTED-NO-RERUN “vein mined out” memory fact remains belief-level on its own (independently re-grounded by the fresh census)
Where this paper goes next The crown paper /papers/ctx-compression-capstone links all five lanes and files the considering-state epic candidate (task-funnel doctrine: considering precedes open). This lane’s done-condition: the user can ratify ONE tier grammar for the whole content model — three layers, two regimes, one binding law — and every epic slice carries the fail-closed proof obligation above. Sibling papers to read with this one: ctx-compression-handle-doctrine (park + handles + the rev grammar law), ctx-compression-taskboard-flagship (the worked example), ctx-compression-headroom-lessons, ctx-compression-spend-census.
